newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl's party says British election ad "unfair".
newsitem.headline: Kohl's party says British election ad "unfair".

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) said on Friday it was unfair of British Conservatives to portray the German leader as a ventriloquist and opposition Labour chief Tony Blair as his diminutive dummy.
The Conservatives, trailing in opinion polls less than two weeks before a general election, placed an advertisement in several British newspapers headed "Labour's Position on Europe".
The advertisement carried a photomontage of the burly chancellor sitting in an armchair and a tiny Blair perched on his knee, both of them beaming.
"It's unfair to bring the German chancellor into the British election campaign like this," CDU general secretary Peter Hintze told Reuters.
"Even allowing for the special nature of the British sense of humour, I don't think it's fair play to deal with the concept of Europe and with a European partner in this way."
Hintze said he had not been in touch with Prime Minister John Major's party about the advertisement, adding the CDU had generally good relations with both Major and the Conservatives.
Peter Hausmann, the chief spokesman for Kohl's centre-right coalition government, adopted a more laid back approach.

"Election campaigns are times when gunsmoke sometimes obscures the landscape," a relaxed Hausmann told reporters at a regular government news conference which attracted a higher than usual attendance from the British press corps.
"The German government will not do anything to judge or pass comment on election campaign events," he said. "Something like that can easily be interpreted as interference."
Referring to major decisions on the reform of the European Union in the offing, the advertisement warned Britons, who vote in the May 1 election: "Don't send a boy to do a man's job."
"This is an internal British affair and not an issue between Britain and Germany," Hausmann said. "It's not our problem."
